title: Splitting and reaping: dividing infinite subsets of omega
summary: Two uncountable minima measure how many subsets are needed to split every infinite set or resist every common splitter.
abstract: A subset of the natural numbers splits an infinite set when it leaves infinitely many points inside and infinitely many outside. Countably many infinite sets always have a common splitter, yet a countable list of proposed splitters always leaves some infinite set undivided. The splitting and reaping numbers measure the smallest families that overcome these two countable limitations. Bounds between them and the existing minima for eventual domination, pseudointersections, and ultrafilter bases show how dividing sets is controlled by approximate containment and the growth of functions.

based_on.title: Combinatorial Cardinal Characteristics of the Continuum
based_on.pages: 7–8 (Definition 2.9 and Theorem 2.10), 9–10 (Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.3), 12–13 (Definition 3.6 and Theorem 3.8); author draft dated November 24, 2003; direct next-point proofs and comparisons with pseudointersections and ultrafilter bases supplied locally
